why: Fix round 1 of slice 15 of the Reflect ban (0554, ticket 1056) in next/ and our tooling, on docs/plan/quests/reflect-ban-PLAN.md law L4 and amendment point 8, on fabrikalfa/reflect-rest from 187b8236a, after the review in field/runs/2026-11-18-reflect-ban-s13-s15-review1.json. oxlint-plugins/advice.test.ts: L4 held what each block of .oxlintrc.json lists, so a glob added to the JSON.parse warn block, which comes after the client/ block, passed it. L4 now holds what each next/ file ends with. It plants one file of fires (JSON.parse, the four Reflect entries, Effect.retry, Stream.retry) in every folder of next/ that holds tracked code, in the stem of every glob of a block that sets the rule, and in a new folder, runs oxlint with the repo's own config, and reads the severity of each fire: that is the last matching override per file, read by oxlint and not by a glob matcher of ours. Each folder must end with JSON.parse and the four restricted at one level, next/ whole, the new folder and client/ with its subfolder at error, and client/ with both retry entries at error. A folder that ends at warn must have a JSON.parse fire in its tree: the real tree is linted with the real config, and the folder one level under a package's src (or src itself, or an app's e2e) that a warn glob is written for must hold a fire, so a glob cannot reach a folder that blocks today and keep the stale warn-line law (T930 L3, per glob) quiet; no list of folders is pinned. Shape 2 of the review: the final setting per file; the config is unchanged and the client/ block stays where it is, so L10's block order is unchanged. A deeper clean folder under a dirty one (node/access under node/**) advises with its parent, as the config has had it, and the law does not hold that.
